definitions.term: Work Done by a Constant Force
definitions.definition: The work done on an object by a constant force is given by $W = F\Delta x\cos\theta$, where $F$ is the magnitude of the force, $\Delta x$ is the magnitude of the displacement, and $\theta$ is the angle between the force and the displacement.
distractors: The work done on an object by a constant force is given by $W = F\Delta x\sin\theta$, where $F$ is the magnitude of the force and $\Delta x$ is the magnitude of the displacement.
The product of the net force acting on an object and the time for which it acts.
The rate at which work is done on an object by a resultant force.
The energy transferred to an object, measured in watts ($W$).
The product of an object's mass and the acceleration caused by the net force.
The amount of heat generated due to friction when an object is displaced by $\Delta x$.

definitions.definition: The net work done on an object is equal to the change in the object's kinetic energy OR the work done on an object by a resultant/net force is equal to the change in the object's kinetic energy.
distractors: The net work done on an object is equal to the change in the object's potential energy.
The total mechanical energy in an isolated system remains constant.
The power output of an object is equal to the change in the object's kinetic energy.
The total work done by all non-conservative forces is equal to zero.
The work done on an object is equal to the product of its mass and its final velocity.
The net work done by conservative forces is equal to the change in mechanical energy.

definitions.definition: A force for which the work done in moving an object between two points is independent of the path taken.
distractors: A force for which the work done in moving an object between two points depends on the path taken.
A force that does not cause any acceleration.
A force that only acts when objects are in direct physical contact.
A force for which the work done in moving an object between two points is always zero.
A force that always acts perpendicular to the direction of motion.
A force that opposes the motion of an object and generates heat.

definitions.definition: A force for which the work done in moving an object between two points depends on the path taken.
distractors: A force for which the work done in moving an object between two points is independent of the path taken.
A force that conserves the total mechanical energy of the system.
A force that only acts over very small distances, such as intermolecular forces.
A force for which the net work done on a closed loop is exactly zero.
A force that acts to increase the kinetic energy of an object to infinity.
The gravitational force exerted by the Earth on any massive object.

definitions.term: Principle of Conservation of Mechanical Energy
definitions.definition: The total mechanical energy in an isolated (closed) system remains constant.
distractors: The total kinetic energy in an isolated system remains constant.
The total work done in an isolated system is zero.
The total potential energy of a closed system always decreases over time.
The total mechanical energy of any system is always conserved, regardless of friction.
The sum of kinetic energy and work done is always constant.
The total energy of a system is conserved only if the object moves vertically.

definitions.definition: The rate at which work is done OR the rate at which energy is expended/transferred.
distractors: The product of the net force acting on an object and its displacement.
The rate of change of momentum of an object.
The total work done over the entire displacement of the object.
The amount of kinetic energy an object possesses per unit mass.
The force required to maintain an object at a constant velocity.
The amount of energy an object has due to its position above the ground.

definitions.definition: The power when one joule of work is done per second ($1\text{ W} = 1\text{ J}\cdot\text{s}^{-1}$).
distractors: The power when one newton of force is applied over one metre ($1\text{ W} = 1\text{ N}\cdot\text{m}$).
The work done when a force of one newton accelerates an object at $1\text{ m\cdot s}^{-2}$.
The energy transferred when one coulomb of charge passes through a potential difference of one volt.
The power output of an object moving at one metre per second squared.
The power when one kilogram of mass is raised by one metre.
The rate at which one joule of kinetic energy is converted into potential energy.

proportionality.statement: If the net work done on an object is positive, its kinetic energy will...
distractors: decrease.
remain constant.
become zero.
increase, then decrease.
fluctuate depending on its mass.
be converted entirely into potential energy.

proportionality.statement: If the net work done on an object is negative, its kinetic energy will...
distractors: increase.
remain constant.
become zero immediately.
fluctuate depending on its mass.
be converted entirely into potential energy.
double.

proportionality.statement: If a force acts perpendicular to the direction of motion of an object, the work done by that force is...
distractors: positive.
negative.
equal to its kinetic energy.
maximum.
equal to the object's potential energy.
dependent on the object's mass.

proportionality.statement: For a vehicle moving at a constant speed, the power output of its engine is directly proportional to...
distractors: the mass of the vehicle.
the time taken for the journey.
the acceleration of the vehicle.
the coefficient of kinetic friction.
the normal force acting on the vehicle.
the square of the vehicle's speed.

concepts.question: Which of the following is an example of a non-conservative force?
distractors: Gravitational force.
Electrostatic force.
Elastic force in a spring.
Magnetic force.
Weight.
The force of gravity acting on a falling object.

concepts.question: Which of the following is an example of a conservative force?
distractors: Air resistance.
Kinetic frictional force.
Tension in a rope.
Applied pushing force.
The driving force of a motor.
Static frictional force.

concepts.question: An object moves at a constant velocity along a rough horizontal surface. What is the net work done on the object?
concepts.correct: Zero, because the change in kinetic energy is zero.
distractors: Positive, because the applied force is greater than the frictional force.
Negative, because friction is doing work against the motion.
Equal to the work done by gravity.
Positive, because the object has a constant kinetic energy.
Equal to the product of its mass and its constant velocity.
Negative, because potential energy is decreasing.
